Definition: from G1223 and G3164; to fight fiercely (in altercation):--strive.
BiblicalUsage: To strive or fight is what the Pharisees and Sadducees do over Paul in the council, contending so fiercely that the captain fears Paul will be torn apart. The word stands only once, and the fight is over the resurrection.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the council's fight is a picture of religion without grace; men who agreed on nothing could agree on tearing Paul apart, and the resurrection they argued over is the very truth that would have united them.
